newsitem.title: USA: Mississippi Chemical looks forward to Q4.
newsitem.headline: Mississippi Chemical looks forward to Q4.

text.p: Mississippi Chemical Corp said Friday it expects to leave its third-quarter troubles behind in the fourth-quarter.
"The adverse events that were experienced during the third quarter are of a non-recurring nature and we are looking forward to the fourth quarter," said president and chief executive Charles Dunn.

"We expect to recover in the fourth quarter much of the weather-related lost nitrogen sales volume. The potash assets are expected to perform significantly better in the fourth quarter due to the improved ore quality and the correction of other operating deficiencies.

"We are confident, based on planting intentions of U.S. farmers, that this will be a good year for fertilizer usage. Since the weather has improved in our trade area, we have experienced a strong recovery in demand," he said.
In the third ended March 31 net income fell to $10.6 million or $0.38 a share from $15.6 million or $0.72.

The company attributed lower third-quarter earnings to prolonged adverse weather conditions in its primary trade area during February and March which resulted in lower than expected sales volumes during the quarter for all upgraded nitrogen products.
The company also experienced production downtime at its newly acquired ammonia plant due to start-up difficulties associated with a major modification of the plant.
The facility overcame the start-up problems and was fully operational by mid-February.
Mississippi also experienced higher production costs at the two potash mines acquired in August 1996 in Carlsbad, N.M., during the quarter.

In addition, the average price for diammonium phosphate was down compared with year-ago levels due to soft international demand. The diammonium phosphate market has firmed recently because of increased U.S. exports to India and other Asian countries, Mississippi said.
